doc.title: Ron Carter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Tour length and Chico's route through better clubs
summary: Carter recalls little of the stops but says Chico's agent found longer club dates in Los Angeles and San Francisco.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Where else did you go? Do you remember any of the hotspots on that tour?
No, man, I know I was glad to get off. (laughs)
It was five months of mostly one-nighters?

Probably one month of one-nighters and a week in California at the club in L.A., my first trip to L.A. … those kinds of … it wasn't always kind of the chitlin' circuit one night routine. There was a nice club in L.A. and we worked in San Francisco for a minute, you know. So it was not the one-nighters that we envision those places at the time to find work. Chico had a nice circuit worked out for himself. He was a well-known guy, he was a famous musician, everybody liked him, and he would find a way to, with an agent … Jack Whittemore, I think, to
be able to find the gigs that were not always one-nighters. You could sit down for many … and rest, so to speak, and get the band to another level.
